summary: macOS: device stuck in recoveryOS with no network after Apple Configurator restore, blocking DEP/MDM enrollment
description:
Issue summary: Multiple corporate MacBook units restored with Apple Configurator (AC2) after an internal firmware prerelease reflash are booting into recoveryOS with no network interfaces available. Devices never reach Setup Assistant and therefore fail DEP/MDM (Intune) enrollment.

Impact: Affected machines cannot be provided to users; onboarding blocked for 8 devices so far (carrier build and standard retail units). Blocking P1 for provisioning queue in US-West.

Environment: macOS 13.6.8 (pre-release firmware applied via AC2), Apple Configurator 2.20.0, corporate DEP (Automated Device Enrollment) + Intune profile push. USB-C Apple Configurator cable workflow from macOS host (Big Sur server host).

Observed behavior: After AC2 restore and firmware reflash, machine boots to a recoveryOS prompt showing Utilities, but ifconfig and networksetup show no active Ethernet or Wi‑Fi hardware. System Information shows PCIe controller present but with no driver; IORegistry entries for airport and en0 are absent. Device never contacts Apple DEP servers.

Expected behavior: Post-restore machines should reach Setup Assistant, enumerate network interfaces, and contact DEP for automated enrollment.

Initial hypothesis: Pre-release firmware image applied by AC2 changed SEP/bridge configuration causing I/O providers for Wi‑Fi/Thunderbolt to not instantiate in recoveryOS. Alternative: AC2 restore workflow using our provisioning host is accidentally applying an OEM factory image (with non-public kext signing) instead of the standard corporate image.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced on two machines (MBP-14,3 and MBA-10,1) using the same AC2 host image.
- When running 'system_profiler SPNetworkDataType' from recovery terminal, network section is empty.
- Checking /Volumes/Recovery/System/Library/Extensions on the mounted recovery image shows missing Apple80211 kext references.
- USB cable logs from host indicate a firmware reflashing step completed with exit 0, but config manifest shows firmware version suffix '-rc1' (we expected '-prod').
- Cross-checked with vendor firmware manifest: vendor accidentally signed an internal RC when tagging the release; AC2 picks image by manifest hash.

Temporary workaround: Pause AC2 restore workflows on the provisioning host; use device-to-device enrollment (user performs setup and enrolls manually) where acceptable. For urgent hires, use previously imaged stock units that were not reflashed.

Proposed fix: Update provisioning host manifest to pin to the confirmed production firmware hash; coordinate with firmware vendor to revoke RC image tag. Add a validation step to AC2 workflow to reject images with '-rc' in version string.

Next steps / action items:
- [Evan Ross] Hold AC2 workflow and tag host image as quarantined (completed 2026-03-12).
- [Aisha Patel] Open vendor escalation with firmware team and request rollback of RC artifact (ticket opened 2026-03-12).
- [OS Team] Add a preflight check to imaging script to validate kext presence in the recovery image.
- [IT Ops] Identify stock pool unaffected by AC2 reflashes for immediate deployments.

Resolution notes: Work in progress — vendor confirmed RC tag was published in error and will publish corrected manifest 2026-03-15. We will resume automated restores after host manifest is updated and preflight validation is added.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Connect Mac to provisioning Mac with Apple Configurator using corporate USB-C cable
2) Select Restore and apply firmware image chosen by provisioning host manifest
3) Wait for AC2 workflow to complete and device to reboot
4) Observe device booting into recoveryOS with no network interfaces and no Setup Assistant
5) From recovery terminal, run 'ifconfig' and 'system_profiler SPNetworkDataType' to confirm absence of network hardware
logs: Recovery terminal: ifconfig -> no en0 or bridge devices listed
